previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and fluid retention, with a plan to undergo right heart catheterization to assess pulmonary pressures. He had gained weight and required 4L of oxygen at night. Due to thrombocytopenia previously linked to Remodulin, dose escalation was not pursued. He was treated with IV diuresis to reduce fluid overload before the procedure. Right heart catheterization revealed improved pulmonary artery systolic pressure at 38 mm Hg, down from 47 mm Hg, with normal filling pressures and preserved cardiac index. His oxygen requirements remained stable. He was discharged home on unchanged medications, including Remodulin at 45 ng/kg/min, furosemide, amiloride, and other home therapies. He was instructed to monitor weight and follow up with specialty care.

Comparison is made with prior study ___.

Cardiomediastinal contours are normal.  There are low lung volumes.  Minimal

INDICATION:  ___ man with hepatitis C, cirrhosis and fevers.  Evaluate
for ascites and mark spot for diagnostic paracentesis.

FINDINGS:  The liver is nodular and heterogeneous in echotexture, compatible
with known cirrhosis.  Doppler assessment of the main portal vein shows
patency and normal hepatopetal flow.  There is no intra-hepatic bile duct
dilation.  The common hepatic duct is dilated to 9 mm, previously 7-8mm on
prior CT, not signficantly changed allowing for differences in technique. The
gallbladder is surgically absent.  The pancreas is not well seen due to
overlying bowel gas.  The spleen is markedly enlarged measuring 23 cm,
previously 18cm on CT ___.  Hyperechoi shadowing foci within the spleen
are calcified granulomas.  Single views of each kidney show no hydronephrosis.
Numerous, markedly enlarged varices as seen on prior CT are redeomstrated. 
The visualized portions of the IVC are normal. No ascites in the abdomen is
noted.

INDICATION: ___ year old man with hep c cirrhosis, portopulmonary hypertension
requiring ___ catheter. 

RADIOLOGISTS: Dr. ___ (resident), Dr. ___ (fellow),
Dr. ___ (attending). Dr ___ was present in the room and monitored
the entire procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  
Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of 200 mcg
fentanyl and 2.5 mg of Versed throughout the total intraservice time of 35
minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored.
Local anesthesia was provided by 1% lidocaine to the dermis and 1% lidocaine
with epinephrine into the subcutaneous tissues.

RADIATION: time 4.0 min, dose 10 mGy.

PROCEDURE: 
Written informed consent was obtained from the patient after explaining the
procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives. 
The patient was transported to the angiography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  The right neck was prepped and draped in usual sterile
fashion. A preprocedure huddle and timeout was performed per ___ protocol.
After anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues a micropuncture needle
was inserted into the right internal jugular vein under ultrasound guidance. 
Hard copy ultrasound images were saved for reference.  A 0.018 nitinol wire
was advanced into the superior vena cava.  After additional anesthesia, a
small ___ was made in the skin.  Micropuncture needle was exchanged with
micropuncture sheath.  The inner cannula and nitinol wire were removed.  A
0.035 J-wire was advanced into the right atrium.  Appropriate measurements
were made for skin incision four fingerbreadths below the venotomy site. The
catheter was determined to have a size of 24 cm. The wire was then advanced
into the IVC. 
Attention was now turned to creation of subcutaneous tunnel.  After additional
local anesthesia, a 1-cm skin incision was made.  A 10 ___ tunneled
catheter was passed from the incision to the venotomy site with aid of metal
tunneling device.  The venotomy tract was dilated with 7 and 9 ___
dilators.  Peel-away sheath was passed over the wire.  The wire and inner
cannula were removed and the catheter was passed through the peel-away sheath.
The peel-away sheath was removed while the catheter was pushed into the right
atrium.  This was confirmed with fluoroscopy demonstrating the catheter tip in
the right atrium.  The single lumen withdrew blood and flushed easily.  The
catheter was secured with ___ silk sutures.  Venotomy site was closed with 2
Vicryl subcuticular stitch.  Dry sterile dressings were applied.  No immediate
post-procedure complications were noted.  The patient tolerated the procedure
well.

IMPRESSION:  
Successful placement of tunneled single lumen 24 cm Hickman catheter via a
right internal jugular vein approach.  The tip is located in the right atrium
and the catheter is ready for use.
